A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same ShadowHack paper with fully readable text, equations, figures, tables and references across 11 pages. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix. The body content matches exactly; the visible difference is the first-page arXiv version/date stamp.

before.justification: Section 5 reports original ShadowHack benchmark results on ISTD+ and SRD, component ablations, and generalization and mask-robustness experiments.

after.justification: Section 5 retains the original benchmark, ablation and robustness results, including ShadowHack's numerical results in Tables 1–5.

M1.justification: The luminance/color decomposition, LRNet, rectified outreach attention, CRNet and checkpoint ensembling in Section 4 are identical. The mask-refinement procedure in Section 5.4 is also unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use ISTD+, SRD, UIUC and UCF, with identical shadow-removal, cross-dataset generalization, inaccurate-mask and selective-mask scenarios.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains identical comparator membership for each dataset, including RASM, Homoformer and ShadowDiffusion. Table 2 and the qualitative comparisons in Figures 7–10 also retain their respective comparator sets.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 retains the same dataset splits, 384×384 training crops, 256×256 evaluation resizing, RGB PSNR/SSIM, LAB RMSE and training settings. Ablation and robustness procedures are unchanged.

E4.justification: Sections 5.3–5.4 preserve the decoupling, attention and CRNet ablations in Tables 3–5, along with the generalization and mask-robustness analyses illustrated in Figures 9–12.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is identical. Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests; Tables 1–5 retain the same point-estimate reporting.

E6.justification: All numerical and qualitative results match. For example, Table 1 reports identical ShadowHack whole-image PSNR/RMSE values of 36.31/2.48 on ISTD+ and 35.94/2.90 on SRD.

T1.justification: Sections 3–4 preserve the image-formation analysis, Retinex assumptions, decomposition definitions and attention equations. Equations 1–13 are unchanged, with no added or revised proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain identical claims about luminance/color decomposition, rectified outreach attention, specialized restoration networks and state-of-the-art shadow-removal performance.

C2.justification: Interpretations of shadow degradation, attention rectification, color recovery, training/testing luminance mismatch and mask robustness are unchanged. No substantive limitations or applicability qualifications are added or removed.

D1.justification: The PyTorch/RTX4090 setup, optimizer, learning rates, augmentations and architectural details in Section 5.1 are identical. Both abstracts retain the same prospective code-release statement and repository link.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion and all 58 references are identical, including positioning relative to Retinex, transformer and diffusion approaches.

P1.justification: The first-page arXiv margin stamp changes from v1, dated 3 Dec 2024, to v3, dated 28 Mar 2025. The title, authors, prose, terminology and section organization remain identical.

P2.justification: All 12 figures and five tables retain identical content, formatting, captions and placement. Rendered pages 2–11 match exactly, and the first-page body layout is unchanged.

improvement.justification: The later PDF reproduces the same scientific content, experimental evidence, explanations and reproducibility information. Updating the arXiv version/date stamp does not meaningfully alter the paper's rigor, clarity or overall quality.
